primers.title: The SamplerOptions tree — and the knob that is not in it
primers.body_md:
`SamplerOptions` is a validated pydantic dataclass, so every field name is checked — and **SamplerV2 has no `resilience_level`**. That knob is EstimatorV2's expectation-value mitigation (TREX at level 1, ZNE at level 2). The blueprint's wording, "set sampler primitive options such as resilience levels", is the bait.

| Level | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| top | `max_execution_time`, `environment`, `simulator`, `default_shots`, `dynamical_decoupling`, `execution`, `twirling`, `experimental` |
| `dynamical_decoupling` | `enable`, `sequence_type` (`XX` default, `XpXm`, `XY4`), `extra_slack_distribution`, `scheduling_method`, `skip_reset_qubits` |
| `twirling` | `enable_gates`, `enable_measure`, `num_randomizations`, `shots_per_randomization`, `strategy` |
| `execution` | `init_qubits`, `rep_delay`, `meas_type` — no `shots`, no `seed_simulator` |
| `simulator` | `noise_model`, `seed_simulator`, `coupling_map`, `basis_gates` |

Learn each knob's DEPTH, not just its name. Misspelled names are rejected; `experimental` is an opt-in dict you fill yourself, not a catch-all for unknown names.

primers.title: Setting options, and where the shot count comes from
primers.body_md:
Untouched options stay `Unset` and take the server default, so behaviour does not drift with the client version.

```python
sampler = SamplerV2(mode=backend, options={"default_shots": 4096})
sampler.options.dynamical_decoupling.enable = True
sampler.options.update(default_shots=1024,
                       dynamical_decoupling={"sequence_type": "XpXm"})
```

All three forms are valid: a mapping or `SamplerOptions` object in the constructor, attribute assignment, or a bulk `update()`; the options object is not read-only. The V1 `sampler.set_options(...)` does NOT exist.

The documented shots precedence:

| Rank | Where the shot count comes from |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | the shot count carried in the PUB's third slot |
| 2 | the `shots=` keyword on `run()` |
| 3 | with twirling on, `num_randomizations` × `shots_per_randomization` |
| 4 | `options.default_shots` |

`shots` must be an integer; a one-element list raises `TypeError`. A local fake backend falls through to 1024; the Runtime service's default is 4096.

primers.title: Nothing to switch off — so roll your own
primers.body_md:
The Sampler is the low-level primitive: it returns the sampled bitstrings shot by shot, with no readout correction. There is no Sampler mitigation to "bypass" by switching it off.

| Technique | Where it lives | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| dynamical decoupling | Sampler, `options.dynamical_decoupling` | suppression: pulse sequences cancel coherent errors on idling qubits |
| Pauli twirling of gates and/or measurements | Sampler, `options.twirling` | suppression: randomizes over an ensemble of equivalent circuits so arbitrary noise becomes Pauli noise |
| TREX, zero-noise extrapolation, PEC, error amplification | Estimator only, `options.resilience.*` or `resilience_level` | mitigation: corrects expectation values |

Neither suppression option rewrites counts into "mitigated" values, and mitigation has no Sampler counterpart: there is no single number to rescale, only a histogram. Code the correction yourself in post-processing.

| Scheme | How it works | Trade-off |
| --- | --- | --- |
| post-selection | drop the shots that violate a known symmetry of the ideal output — a Bell circuit can only produce `00` or `11` — then renormalize over what survives | cheap and needs no calibration, but only works when the ideal support is known, and it throws information away |
| assignment-matrix (confusion-matrix) inversion | prepare each computational basis state with calibration circuits, record what you read back, assemble the matrix mapping true outcomes to observed ones, and invert it (or least-squares invert it) | rigorous; this is what packages such as M3/mthree automate, and the raw per-shot record is exactly their input |

Post-process the `BitArray`: faster than round-tripping through `get_counts()`.

primers.title: PUBs, shots, and broadcasting
primers.body_md:
The Sampler runs a circuit many times, recording the measured register each shot — draws from the circuit's distribution over computational-basis states. It never returns amplitudes or expectation values; probabilities are frequencies you compute, with statistical error shrinking like 1/√N_shots, so halving the error costs four times the shots.

Input is a **PUB** (Primitive Unified Bloc): a tuple of at most three entries, `(circuit, parameter_values, shots)`, the last two optional. The circuit must contain measurements; `run()` takes a LIST of PUBs.

```python
result = sampler.run([(isa, params, 200)])   # never run(isa)
# (isa, 256, vals)     -> TypeError: shots must be an integer
# (isa, vals, 200, 1)  -> ValueError: The length of pub must be 1, 2 or 3
```

Binding follows NumPy broadcasting plus one rule: the parameter array's LAST axis holds the circuit's free parameters and is consumed; the shape before it becomes the result's shape.

| Parameter array (circuit has 2 parameters) | `data.meas.shape` |
| --- | --- |
| `(6, 2)` | `(6,)` |
| `(3, 4, 2)` | `(3, 4)`, indexable as `data.meas[i, j]` |
| `(5, 3)` | `ValueError: Length of ('p[0]', 'p[1]') inconsistent with last dimension` |

Transposing, flattening or splitting into one PUB per row all raise that same error; reshaping to `(5, 2)` is the fix.

primers.title: Reading a SamplerPubResult
primers.body_md:
`run()` returns a `PrimitiveResult` with one entry per PUB, in submission order.

| Access path | What you get |
| --- | --- |
| `len(result)` | the number of PUBs submitted — three circuits in one `run()` give three PUB results |
| `result[0].data` | a `DataBin` holding one `BitArray` per classical register, named after the register (`data.alice`, `data.bob`) |
| `.get_counts()` | the histogram, as a plain `dict` |
| `.get_int_counts()` | the same histogram with the bitstrings decoded as integers (`'11'` becomes the key `3`) |
| `.get_bitstrings()` | the raw per-shot list, in the order the shots were taken |
| `.get_counts(0)` on a broadcast result | that one parameter set's 500 shots; with no index, `get_counts()` POOLS every set (4 × 500 = 2000) |

Only `measure_all()` creates a register called `meas`. The per-shot view lets you correlate outcomes across registers before aggregating; a counts dict cannot.

facts.fact_md: Settable on SamplerV2: `options.default_shots`, `options.dynamical_decoupling.enable`, `options.twirling.enable_gates`; `resilience_level` and `optimization_level` both fail validation.
A PUB shot count beats the option: with `options.default_shots = 1000`, the PUB `(isa, None, 50)` runs exactly 50 shots.
`sampler.options.resilience_level = 1` raises a pydantic `ValidationError` ("Object has no attribute 'resilience_level'"); the constructor's `options={...}` mapping rejects it too.
Configuring is not enabling: dynamical decoupling needs `options.dynamical_decoupling.enable = True`; setting only `sequence_type` is accepted but leaves `enable` Unset.
The simulator seed lives at `options.simulator.seed_simulator`; `options.execution.seed_simulator`, top-level `seed_simulator`, `run(seed=42)` and `run(options={...})` are all rejected.
`SamplerV2(mode=backend, options={"default_shots": 4096})` is the constructor form; a `"shots"` key is rejected, and `SamplerV2(shots=...)` or `(default_shots=...)` is a `TypeError`.
`twirling_level` and `readout` are not `twirling` fields; those near-miss names fail validation.
Post-selection is code you write: a Bell run's raw counts `{'00': 1941, '11': 1822, '01': 90, '10': 147}` become `{'00': 1941, '11': 1822}` by dropping odd-parity shots and renormalizing.
A `BitArray` supports boolean-mask post-selection on another register, `slice_bits`, `slice_shots`, `expectation_values` for diagonal observables, and `concatenate_bits` to merge registers.
Shots are per parameter set, not per PUB: 6 parameter values with `shots=200` make 6 × 200 = 1200 circuit executions.
`get_counts()` values sum to the shot count (`shots=1000` → 1000) however many distinct bitstrings appear.
Bitstrings are little-endian: qubit 0 is the LAST character, so read `b[-1]`, not `b[0]`; after `x(0)` on two qubits the dominant outcome is `'01'`.
Runtime `SamplerV2` rejects a non-ISA circuit with `IBMInputValueError`; the fix is transpiling with a preset pass manager for the backend, not changing the run call.
The reference `StatevectorSampler` in `qiskit.primitives` accepts abstract (non-ISA) instructions, since it simulates a local statevector — the ISA requirement is a Runtime-primitive rule.
`result[0].data.meas` is a `BitArray` of per-shot outcomes, not a counts dict; `get_counts()` gives the summary as a plain `dict`.
`QuantumCircuit(2, 2)` names its register `c`, so outcomes are in `data.c`; `meas` exists only after `measure_all()`.

`get_counts()` lists only outcomes that occurred: a 40-shot two-qubit run that never produced `10` gives a three-key dict, so `plot_histogram` draws three bars — no zero-height bar for the missing outcome.
A fake backend is not an exact simulator: a seeded 2000-shot `h(0); cx(0,1); x(2)` run on FakeManilaV2 hits all eight outcomes, the ideal peaks `100` and `111` holding about 43% and 40% of shots.
`join_data()` puts the FIRST-declared register at the low-index, rightmost end: `out` (reads `10`) declared before `anc` (reads `1`) joins to `'110'`; `join_data(['anc', 'out'])` gives `'101'`.

`StatevectorSampler` rejects dynamic circuits: an `if_test` raises `QiskitError: 'StatevectorSampler cannot handle ControlFlowOp'`, a reset or gate after a measurement `'... cannot handle mid-circuit measurements'`. Use `SamplerV2(mode=AerSimulator())` instead.

`BitArray.postselect(indices, selection)` takes BIT indices (0 is the rightmost character, as in `slice_bits`) and `selection` lists values to KEEP: on `000`/`111`/`100`/`011`, `postselect([2], [0])` keeps only `000` and `011`, still 3 bits.

checklist: Place each SamplerV2 knob at its level (`dynamical_decoupling`, `twirling`, `execution`, `simulator`); SamplerV2 has no `resilience_level`.
Enable a technique explicitly; setting only `sequence_type` leaves `enable` Unset.
Recite the shots precedence: PUB slot, `run(shots=)`, twirling randomizations, `options.default_shots`.
Hand `run()` a LIST of PUBs, each at most `(circuit, parameter_values, shots)`, circuits measured.
Derive the result shape: the parameter array's last axis binds parameters, leading axes survive.
Read outcomes from the register-named `BitArray`; `data.meas` exists only after `measure_all()`.
Read every bitstring right-to-left — qubit 0 is the last character.
Build readout correction yourself (post-selection or assignment-matrix inversion); the Sampler ships none.
